t: LeetCode 2015 — Average Height of Buildings in Each Segment
o:
## Understanding the problem

Each building covers the half-open interval [start, end) with a given height. We must re-describe the street as the fewest disjoint half-open segments, each labeled with the average height (total height divided by number of buildings, integer division) of all buildings covering it, skipping uncovered stretches. Output order is free.

Example walkthrough: [[1,5,2],[3,10,4]] — on [1,3) only building one stands: average 2/1 = 2; on [3,5) both stand: (2+4)/2 = 3; on [5,10) only building two: 4/1 = 4. Result: [[1,3,2],[3,5,3],[5,10,4]]. Note building one ends exactly where coverage changes — half-open semantics mean the point 5 belongs to no segment of building one.

Constraints: up to 10^5 buildings with coordinates up to 10^8, so materializing every unit position is impossible; only building boundaries matter, and sums reach 10^5 × 10^5 = 10^10, requiring 64-bit accumulation.
k: Coverage and average height are constant between consecutive building endpoints — only boundaries matter.
Sweep events: +height,+1 at each start and −height,−1 at each end; between consecutive events the street is uniform.
Merge adjacent output segments sharing an average — minimality demands it; gaps (coverage zero) must be skipped.

a.n: Approach 1: Coordinate compression with per-interval rescans
a.i: Collect and sort all distinct endpoints; between consecutive endpoints the street is uniform. For each elementary interval, rescan every building to accumulate covered height sum and count, then merge the result with the previous output segment if averages match. Clear and correct, but each of the O(B) elementary intervals pays an O(B) scan.
s: Gather all starts and ends, deduplicate, sort.
For each consecutive pair (s, e): sum heights and count of buildings with start <= s and e <= end.
Append [s, e, sum // count], merging into the previous segment when it ends at s with the same average.
a.t: O(B^2) after O(B log B) sorting — each elementary interval rescans all buildings

a.i: Record net deltas at each boundary: +height,+1 at a start and −height,−1 at the corresponding end, collected in a sorted map. Sweeping boundaries in order, close out the current segment before applying a boundary delta, then apply it. Between events, average = running total / running count; merge segments whose averages match and whose positions touch. Each building touches exactly two events, so the whole thing runs in O(B log B).
s: Build a map pos -> (deltaHeight, deltaCount) from all starts and ends.
Iterate positions ascending; before applying the delta at p, if count > 0 emit or merge the segment [prev, p, total // count].
a.t: O(B log B) — sorting/map ordering dominates; each building creates two events

w:
## Wrap-up

This is a classic difference-array / sweep-line problem; in interviews describe the event sweep directly, keeping the compression-rescan version as the warm-up. As pure SQL (its native database form) the same idea uses UNION ALL events plus a windowed cumulative sum with LAG-based run detection for merging. Pitfalls: applying the end-delta before closing the segment ending at that coordinate (half-open intervals mean the end point belongs to the next segment, not the current one); merging across a coverage gap just because averages match; forgetting minimality requires merging adjacent equal-average segments; overflowing 32-bit totals (up to 10^10). Edge cases: touching buildings ([1,3) and [3,6) never overlap at point 3), duplicated identical ranges, fully disjoint buildings. Follow-ups: the skyline problem (max instead of average, needing a multiset), streaming insertions, or returning segments sorted by start.
